note: Hand-maintained, unlike data/index.json. The reader marks the first occurrence of each term in each section and shows this on click. Keys match case-sensitively on whole words, so only add genuinely opaque abbreviations: US, EU and UN are noise, not help. Where an abbreviation has a common other meaning, say so in the gloss — that is the case this file earns its keep on. "wikipedia" is an exact article title, verified against the Wikipedia API rather than guessed; false where no article is worth linking; omitted where none exists but a search still helps, in which case the reader searches on the expansion.

AOSIS.gloss: The negotiating bloc of low-lying and island states. Its leverage rests almost entirely on 1.5°C being a commitment rather than a target, which is why it fights framing changes to that number.

AIIB.gloss: The Beijing-headquartered multilateral development bank. A lender, which matters when a climate-justice argument is taken to it.

BIM.gloss: The Loss and Damage Fund's interim route to money, financing country-led projects of $5 to $20 million while the fund tests approaches for its longer-term operations. Not a response mechanism for a specific disaster.

BRIC.gloss: A FEMA pre-disaster mitigation grant programme. Nothing to do with the BRICS grouping of states.

CCS.gloss: A US institute, now part of the Council on Strategic Risks. In most other writing CCS means carbon capture and storage; in this digest it does not.

CNA.gloss: A US non-profit research organisation, formerly the Center for Naval Analyses. Its 2007 Military Advisory Board report put "threat multiplier" into circulation.

COP.gloss: The decision-making body of a UN convention. Which convention depends on context: usually the climate convention, but the desertification and biodiversity conventions have their own numbered COPs.

COP31.expansion: 31st Conference of the Parties to the UN climate convention

CPS.gloss: The UN system's own term for the field, and the job title of the advisers it deploys.

CRS.gloss: The US Congress's in-house research arm.

CSDP.gloss: The EU's framework for military and civilian crisis-management missions.

CSM.gloss: The joint UN unit run by DPPA, UNDP, UNEP and DPO. The field's only standing multilateral machinery.

CSR.gloss: The US institute that houses the Center for Climate and Security.

CWP.gloss: The European Commission's annual list of what it intends to propose, and when.

D66.gloss: Dutch social-liberal party; leads the cabinet sworn in February 2026.

DG CLIMA.gloss: The European Commission department that owns the climate file.

DHS.wikipedia: United States Department of Homeland Security

DPO.wikipedia: United Nations Department of Peace Operations

DPPA.expansion: UN Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs
DPPA.wikipedia: United Nations Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs

EAM.gloss: India's foreign minister — the office, not the ministry. MEA in these digests is the ministry itself; EAM is the person who runs it.

EEAS.gloss: The EU's diplomatic service, and where its climate-security file sits.

ENSO.gloss: The Pacific climate oscillation behind El Niño and La Niña. Its dry teleconnections, not its wet ones, carry most of the measured conflict risk.

ENVI.expansion: Committee on the Environment, Climate and Food Safety
ENVI.gloss: The European Parliament's environment committee, renamed in 2024 when public health moved to a committee of its own. Which committee hears a security-framed climate argument is itself a finding: ENVI's competence is environmental regulation, not security or defence.
ENVI.wikipedia: European Parliament Committee on the Environment, Climate and Food Safety

FEMA.gloss: The US disaster response and mitigation agency.

FRLD.expansion: Fund for responding to Loss and Damage
FRLD.gloss: The fund's own name for itself, usually called the Loss and Damage Fund. Its board is where a claim arising from a specific disaster is decided.

GHACOF.expansion: Greater Horn of Africa Climate Outlook Forum
GHACOF.gloss: The regional seasonal-forecast forum, numbered by session.

GLOF.gloss: A flood caused by a glacier-dammed lake draining suddenly. Monitoring in the Himalaya is built around this hazard, which is why an ice-and-rock avalanche can arrive unwatched.

HCSS.expansion: The Hague Centre for Strategic Studies
HCSS.wikipedia: The Hague Centre for Strategic Studies

HiRISK.gloss: A self-described loose consortium of High Mountain Asia risk experts producing open datasets, dashboards and risk assessments. Not an institute, not a funded programme, and not the initials of a longer official name — which is why establishing its membership and funding took two weeks.

ICIMOD.expansion: International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development
ICIMOD.gloss: The intergovernmental body for the Hindu Kush Himalaya, based in Kathmandu.
ICIMOD.wikipedia: International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development

IMCCS.expansion: International Military Council on Climate and Security

IenW.gloss: The Dutch Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management, which holds the water file and the Deltafonds.
IenW.wikipedia: Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management

IOD.gloss: A sea-surface temperature oscillation across the Indian Ocean; both its phases raise conflict risk in strongly connected regions.

IWT.gloss: The 1960 India–Pakistan water-sharing treaty brokered by the World Bank.

KNMI.gloss: The Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute, and one of the partners behind World Weather Attribution.

MEA.gloss: India's foreign ministry. In environmental writing MEA usually means multilateral environmental agreement; here it does not.

MFF.gloss: The EU's seven-year budget. The 2028–2034 round proposes 35 per cent climate and environment mainstreaming, which is not the same as a climate-security line.

MPTF.gloss: The UN pooled-funding vehicle through which member states finance joint programmes.

NASEM.expansion: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
NASEM.gloss: The US academies' advisory body. Its consensus study reports are about as authoritative as a scientific review gets, which makes the questions they decline to take up consequential.
NASEM.wikipedia: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine

NDC.gloss: A country's self-set emissions pledge under the Paris Agreement.

NDRRMA.expansion: National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority
NDRRMA.gloss: Nepal's disaster agency, and the source of its official casualty figures.
NDRRMA.wikipedia: National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority

NDS.gloss: The US Department of Defense's periodic strategy document.

NIC.gloss: The US intelligence community's long-range analytic body; publisher of Global Trends.

NOFO.gloss: The instrument that actually releases US federal grant money, so its issue date is when a programme becomes real.

NSIDC.expansion: National Snow and Ice Data Center
NSIDC.wikipedia: National Snow and Ice Data Center

NSR.gloss: The Arctic shipping route along Russia's northern coast.

OND.gloss: The short rains season in the eastern Horn of Africa, forecast as a unit.

PCA.gloss: The inter-state arbitration institution seated in The Hague.

PDD.gloss: NATO's communications arm, and the office to ask when a NATO publication quietly stops appearing.

PDNA.gloss: The standard consolidated assessment of a disaster's physical, economic and human toll and the recovery it requires. Donors routinely make their decisions conditional on it, so its publication date is when the money becomes discussable.

PGA80.expansion: President of the 80th session of the UN General Assembly
PGA80.wikipedia: President of the United Nations General Assembly

PIF.gloss: The regional body of Pacific states; author of the Boe Declaration and the Ocean of Peace Declaration.

PNAS.expansion: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
PNAS.wikipedia: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

PSC.gloss: The African Union's standing decision-making organ for conflict prevention and response.

PSI.gloss: The Dutch-founded climate-security platform hosted at Clingendael.

RDNA.gloss: The fast, preliminary version of a post-disaster assessment, produced within weeks. Its figures are the ones quoted while the fuller assessment is still being written, and they move.

SAS-182.expansion: Systems Analysis and Studies research task group 182
SAS-182.gloss: The NATO Science and Technology Organization group behind The Effects of Climate Change on Security, January 2026.

SCP.gloss: The Netherlands Institute for Social Research, the government's own social research agency and the best source on Dutch climate opinion. Not to be confused with SCR below, which is an NGO tracking the UN Security Council.
SCP.wikipedia: The Netherlands Institute for Social Research

SCR.gloss: The independent organisation that tracks UN Security Council business. Not a Security Council resolution.

SRM.gloss: Deliberate cooling by reflecting sunlight. Its governance is where the security frame appears to be travelling next.

UNCCD.wikipedia: United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification

UNEP.gloss: The UN's environmental authority, based in Nairobi.

UNGA81.expansion: 81st session of the UN General Assembly
UNGA81.gloss: Opened 8 September 2026; high-level week from 22 September.

UNISFA.expansion: UN Interim Security Force for Abyei
UNISFA.wikipedia: United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei

WWA.gloss: The research network that publishes rapid studies on whether climate change made a given extreme event more likely.

VVD.wikipedia: People's Party for Freedom and Democracy

ITU.gloss: The UN agency that allocates radio spectrum and sets telecommunication standards. In these digests it appears twice over and in tension with itself: as the forum where the frequency bands weather satellites depend on are contested, and as the COP31 presidency's partner on an artificial-intelligence pledge.

WRC-27.gloss: The treaty conference that revises the international radio regulations, including the bands protected for meteorological observation. Held roughly every four years.

SAI.gloss: The most-discussed form of solar radiation modification: injecting reflective particles into the stratosphere to reduce incoming sunlight. Not deployed anywhere.

CERF.gloss: The UN's central pooled humanitarian fund, which since 2020 also pre-approves money for anticipatory action against a forecast rather than an observed disaster. Not a country-level pooled fund, which is a different instrument.

IEA.gloss: The Paris-based energy body of the OECD. Not the Institute of Economic Affairs, which shares the initials and appears in British debate on the same subjects.

ELM.gloss: Specifically the India-China Expert Level Mechanism on Trans-Border Rivers, set up in 2006, which handles flood-season hydrological data sharing on the Brahmaputra and Sutlej. A generic-sounding name for the only standing bilateral channel on Himalayan river data.

IPCC.gloss: The UN body that assesses published climate science rather than conducting it. These digests usually call it the climate panel; the abbreviation appears in citations. Not to be confused with the IPC below, which is a food-security scale.

AR7.gloss: The climate panel's next full assessment cycle, whose timetable is the thing five of its plenary sessions have failed to agree. The three working-group reports and the synthesis report are separately scheduled, and only the working-group reports are in dispute.

IPC.gloss: The five-phase scale on which food crises are classified, Phase 5 being Famine at area level and Catastrophe at household level. A different thing from the IPCC above, and from the patent and industrial-computing classifications that share the letters.

FAO.gloss: The UN agency, Rome. Its Somalia water and land unit, SWALIM below, is the source of the seasonal flood probabilities in these pages.

SWALIM.expansion: Somalia Water and Land Information Management
SWALIM.gloss: FAO's Somalia water and land monitoring unit, which issues the river-basin and seasonal rainfall assessments the Deyr flood forecasts rest on.

UNIDIR.wikipedia: United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research

BCSC.gloss: The German Federal Foreign Office's annual climate-security convening, held with adelphi since 2019. It has no standing output document.

ENCOP.gloss: A 1990s joint project of the Swiss Peace Foundation and the Zurich federal technical university, led by Günther Bächler with Kurt Spillmann, whose final report was published in 1996. Frequently cited as shorthand for Bächler's 1999 monograph, which is a different publication by a different publisher.

NCQG.expansion: New Collective Quantified Goal on Climate Finance
NCQG.gloss: The post-2025 climate finance goal agreed at Baku in 2024: at least US$300 billion a year by 2035, inside a wider call to mobilise US$1.3 trillion a year. "Quantified" refers to the collective goal, not to any country's share of it.

InSAR.gloss: Comparing successive satellite radar passes to measure ground movement to centimetre precision. It measures displacement along the satellite's line of sight rather than true three-dimensional motion — which is why the Himalayan slope figure is quoted as line-of-sight movement.

CELAC.expansion: Community of Latin American and Caribbean States
CELAC.wikipedia: Community of Latin American and Caribbean States

IPCS.expansion: Institute of Peace and Conflict Studies, New Delhi
IPCS.gloss: An Indian research institute. Not the climate panel (IPCC) and not the food-security classification scale (IPC), both of which also appear in these digests and neither of which it is.

LDCs.gloss: The UN's formal category of forty-odd states on defined income, human-asset and vulnerability criteria — a negotiating bloc as well as a classification, and in climate texts usually paired with the small island states as the group entitled to particular treatment.

AUPSC.expansion: African Union Peace and Security Council
AUPSC.gloss: The African Union's standing security organ. Elsewhere in these digests the same body is abbreviated PSC; both appear because sources use both.

CCASCOE.expansion: Climate Change and Security Centre of Excellence
CCASCOE.gloss: NATO's climate centre of excellence, in Montreal, with Canada as framework nation. A distinct body from NATO headquarters and from the alliance's Science and Technology Organization, and it publishes separately.

IOM.gloss: The UN migration agency. Not to be confused with the Isle of Man, for which the same letters are the usual abbreviation.

NEMA.gloss: Nigeria's federal disaster agency, which publishes a public flood dashboard. Several other countries have a body of the same name and abbreviation.
